h1: The 6 Best Printers for Homeschooling of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six printers for homeschool families, from refillable ink tanks to a mono laser, sorted by running cost and scanning.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is the best printer for homeschooling, because bottled ink keeps daily printing cheap. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick for black-and-white curricula, and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 suits parents who scan graded work. The HP Smart Tank 5101 and DeskJet 4355 are budget routes with tradeoffs.
intro: A homeschool printer's real price is revealed in the second semester. A curriculum that prints 20 to 40 pages a day turns a cheap cartridge machine into the costliest object in the house, because the discount on the hardware is paid back in ink. How a printer stores and charges for ink matters far more than which apps it supports.

We ranked six printers that fit a kitchen table or a school shelf, judging them on paper from spec sheets and owner reports. Running cost, duplex printing, scanning with a document feeder and wireless setup counted most. Prices are shown as buckets because they move constantly, and an idle-friendly design was a plus, since summer breaks dry out neglected inkjets.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: The printer that stops ink from being your biggest homeschool expense.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is a cartridge-free color printer, scanner and copier that refills from bottles, ships with ink included and connects by Wi-Fi. Bottled ink costs a fraction of cartridge pricing per page, so a family printing worksheets every week stops watching the ink gauge.

It ranks first because it fixes the expense that sinks most homeschool printers. The Brother laser is cheaper per page for text, but only prints black. The Canon and Epson WF-2930 add feeders at the cost of cartridge ink.

Buy it if you print color and black-and-white pages every week. The caveats are no listed document feeder and a higher upfront cost, so skip it if you print only a handful of pages a month.
products.idealFor: Families printing color and black-and-white pages every week.
products.skipIf: You print a handful of pages a month.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser
products.verdict: A text-first workhorse that never dries out between school terms.
products.description:
Brother's DCP-L2640DW goes all-in on black text: a laser engine, automatic two-sided printing, copy and scan, and wireless and mobile printing from a body small enough for a school desk. Toner does not dry out, so after a summer off the printer still works on the first morning of term. Duplex halves paper use on thick packets.

It ranks second because it prints only black and white and sits in the highest price bucket here. The EcoTank wins when lessons need color maps or diagrams.

Buy it for text-heavy curricula with daily worksheets. Skip it if your lessons rely on color printouts. Skim your curriculum's sample pages first, because science and art units often assume color.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy curricula with daily black-and-white worksheets.
products.skipIf: Your lessons rely on color printouts.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: The affordable pick for parents who archive every graded page.
products.description:
Canon's PIXMA TR4720 is a budget color inkjet that feeds its scanner from a stack tray, prints wirelessly from phones and tablets, and keeps a legacy fax built in. A feeder lets a parent scan a stack of graded worksheets without lifting the lid for each page, which matters when you archive records.

It ranks third because cartridge ink adds up at homeschool volumes, and fax is a legacy extra. It costs far less up front than the EcoTank, which suits trial-year budgets.

Buy it if you scan stacks of graded work. Skip it if you print more than a few dozen pages weekly. For heavy printing, the ink bill will eventually exceed the savings on the machine.
products.idealFor: Parents who scan stacks of graded worksheets.
products.skipIf: You print more than a few dozen pages weekly.

products.name: Epson Workforce WF-2930 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Duplex and a feeder on one budget inkjet, with cartridge ink as the price.
products.description:
Epson's Workforce WF-2930 prints on both sides of the page automatically and also feeds multi-page scans, with a 1.4 inch color display and a cartridge-based ink system. Duplex plus a feeder is rare at this price, and it covers packets as well as scans.

It ranks fourth because cartridge ink costs more than the tank models, and the control display is tiny. It beats the Canon TR4720 on duplex, which the Canon listing does not mention.

Buy it for moderate printing with paper-saving duplex and multi-page scans. Skip it if you print heavy color every day. A busy household will feel the cartridge cost within a term.
products.idealFor: Moderate printing with paper-saving duplex and multi-page scans.
products.skipIf: You print heavy color every day.

products.award: Best Ink Tank on a Tight Budget
products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless All-in-One Refillable Printer
products.verdict: Tank-style savings with a small footprint, minus a document feeder.
products.description:
The HP Smart Tank 5101 is a refillable-tank all-in-one that ships with two years of ink, printing, scanning and copying over 2.4GHz Wi-Fi. Two years of ink offsets the premium that tank printers usually carry, and the compact body fits a small desk.

It ranks fifth because it has no document feeder and works only on the 2.4GHz band. It beats the DeskJet on running cost, but trails the EcoTank on documented ink supply.

Buy it for tank savings on a tighter budget. Skip it if your router offers only a combined 5GHz network. Check the Wi-Fi band before ordering, because the printer simply will not connect on 5GHz.
products.idealFor: Tank savings for a family on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: Your router only offers a combined 5GHz network.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A low-risk way to learn your real print volume first.
products.description:
HP's DeskJet 4355 is a compact, low-cost starter that prints, scans and copies over Wi-Fi and includes a three-month Instant Ink trial. As a first printer, it lets you learn your actual page count before you commit to a tank model.

It ranks last because there is no feeder listed and cartridge ink adds up. The trial is a subscription, so read the terms before you enroll.

Buy it as a low-risk starter for new homeschoolers testing real print volume. Skip it if you already print daily, because the running cost will outpace the savings. Once your volume is clear, move to the EcoTank, which suits steady weekly printing.
products.idealFor: New homeschoolers testing their real print volume.

whatMatters.detail: Cartridge printers sell hardware cheaply and make money on refills, while tank printers use bottled ink that costs far less per page. For a family printing daily, that gap outweighs the upfront price. Check the listing for words like refillable, tank or EcoTank rather than assuming a printer is economical, and count how many pages you really print each week.

A monochrome laser is excellent for text but prints every diagram in gray. Decide whether your curriculum truly needs color science, maps and art pages, because that settles laser versus ink. Skim your curriculum's sample pages before deciding. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is mono only, while the EcoTank and HP models print color for a fraction of the cartridge price.

A feeder pulls a stack of sheets through the scanner so you do not lift the lid for each page. It matters when you scan graded work for records. Look for the words automatic document feeder in the specs, since many models skip it entirely. The Canon TR4720 and Epson WF-2930 list one; the EcoTank ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank do not.

Automatic two-sided printing halves paper use and shortens thick packets. Manual duplex means flipping pages yourself, which wastes time over a school year. Look for automatic 2-sided in the listing. The Brother DCP-L2640DW and Epson WF-2930 list it, while the Canon and HP DeskJet list none.

Some tank printers connect only on the 2.4GHz band, which trips up routers that combine bands under one name. Check your router settings before purchase. The listing usually states the band in the feature bullets. The HP Smart Tank 5101 is the model here that states 2.4GHz only.

faq.q: Is a laser or inkjet better for homeschooling?
faq.a: A laser such as the Brother DCP-L2640DW is better for black-and-white text because toner stays usable between school terms. An inkjet or ink tank is better when you need color, and the EcoTank keeps color affordable.

faq.q: Do I need a document feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan stacks of graded work. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 and Epson Workforce WF-2930 list feeders. For single pages and the odd worksheet, a flatbed on the EcoTank ET-2400 does the job.

faq.q: Is an ink tank printer worth it over a cheap inkjet?
faq.a: If you print weekly, yes. The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 costs more upfront, but bottled ink is far cheaper than cartridges. If you print rarely, a cheap inkjet like the DeskJet 4355 is enough.

faq.q: Why won't my HP Smart Tank 5101 connect?
faq.a: It works on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi only. Turn on the 2.4GHz band on your router or separate the band names during setup, and then add the printer again from the HP app, which restores the connection.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles from clogging?
faq.a: Print a color page every week or two. Long idle spells are where inkjets suffer and lasers do not, which is why the Brother laser suits a family that pauses for summer.

faq.q: Can I use these with an iPad?
faq.a: Most list wireless and mobile printing. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 specifically mentions mobile printing support. Check the app for your tablet and your printer before relying on it for daily lessons, and test one print before term starts.

finalTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2400 is the right homeschool printer for most families, because ink stops being the biggest recurring expense. Choose the Brother DCP-L2640DW for text-only curricula and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 if you archive graded work. Learn your page volume first, then decide how much to pay.
